extraction.title: Add Memory
extraction.guideTitle: Enter something you want the system to remember
extraction.guideDescription: MindMemOS can extract facts, lessons, constraints, error reflections, and domain knowledge from natural language. Tags are inferred automatically when possible and can be edited after saving. Avoid context-free fragments, temporary chat, or sensitive secrets.
extraction.placeholder: Include the scenario, conclusion, reason or evidence, and reusable guidance. Example: in this project, algorithms should prioritize stability and interpretability; an overly large mutation rate caused population degradation, so future runs should start with a smaller range.

algorithm.label: Algorithm Lesson
algorithm.content: For small and medium TSP instances, 2-opt local search works well as a post-processing operator and often improves nearest-neighbor initial solutions. For larger instances, limit the candidate neighborhood to avoid excessive evaluation time per round.

reflection.label: Error Reflection
reflection.content: In the previous evolutionary search, setting mutation rate above 0.2 quickly reduced population diversity, damaged strong individuals, and worsened convergence. For similar tasks, start by testing the 0.01 to 0.05 range.

domain.label: Domain Knowledge
domain.content: This task values algorithm stability, interpretability, and reproducible results. Only consider complex black-box strategies when the gain is clear, and compare variance, failure rate, and average performance first.

general.label: General Practice
general.content: When a heuristic has several tightly coupled parameters, fix the operator combination first, tune parameters group by group, and record each ablation's benefit and side effects so changes remain attributable.

constraints.label: Project Constraints
constraints.content: This project prioritizes stability, interpretability, and reproducible experiments. Introduce complex black-box strategies or expensive search operators only when the gain is clear and the failure rate remains controlled.

evaluation.label: Evaluation Preference
evaluation.content: When comparing algorithms in this project, prioritize average performance, variance, failure rate, and runtime. A single best run is only supporting evidence and should not replace conclusions from repeated stability checks.

algorithm.label: Reusable Algorithm Pattern
algorithm.content: For TSP-like tasks in this project, a nearest-neighbor initial solution followed by 2-opt over a restricted candidate neighborhood has been stable. As instance size grows, limit the neighborhood size to keep evaluation cost under control.

reflection.label: Project Error Lesson
reflection.content: An overly high mutation rate in this project previously damaged strong individuals and worsened convergence. For similar tasks, first run ablations in the 0.01 to 0.05 range before expanding the search.

retrieval.autoHint: The system automatically retrieves and injects global and project memory.
retrieval.manualHint: You manually select fixed memories to inject; shared memory is not auto-retrieved at runtime.

injectionCount.help: The injection count controls how many global/project memories are injected per prompt. Higher values give richer context but use more prompt space.

manualPicker.empty: No memory cards available in this scope.

injection.label: Task Memory Injection Mode
injection.help: Task memory is produced during a run. It is always retrieved first, then injected according to the mode below.
injection.topkHelp: Order by retrieval relevance and inject the top N most relevant.
injection.weightHelp: Order by the per-memory weight you set in memory management.
injection.randomHelp: Randomly inject from the retrieved candidates for more diversity.
injection.taskLimitHelp: Maximum number of task memories injected per prompt.
injection.lambdaHelp: Injection weight = λ×similarity + (1-λ)×recency. Higher λ favors relevance, lower favors freshness.

memoryConfig.searchStrategyHelp: fast is suitable for normal retrieval. agentic plans retrieval more actively and may take longer.
memoryConfig.scoreThresholdHelp: Only effective when rerank is enabled; filters low-relevance reranked memories.
memoryConfig.requestTimeoutHelp: Maximum wait time for one search request. Leave empty or enter 0 to wait indefinitely. After timeout, Fail-open decides whether to continue or fail.
memoryConfig.addTimeoutHelp: Maximum wait time for one extraction/write request. Task memory creation is usually slower than search, default 120 seconds. Leave empty or enter 0 to wait indefinitely.
memoryConfig.extractionLanguageHelp: Controls the extraction language for task runtime writes and new memory creation. Auto uses the default.
memoryConfig.rerankHelp: Rerank recalled memories to improve relevance before injection.
memoryConfig.rerankUnavailable: System-level rerank is not enabled, so this task cannot enable reranking.
memoryConfig.failOpenHelp: Continue running the task when long-term memory is temporarily unavailable, skipping remote memory to avoid interruption.

projects.demoContent: Click this read-only example to walk through a full algorithm-design run in seconds. No LLM keys needed.
projects.createProjectContent: Click the "New Project" button to create a project. Projects help you organize and manage your algorithm design tasks.
projects.configProviderContent: In the left sidebar under "LLM Providers", you can configure global LLM providers (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic). These configurations are shared across all projects.

evolutionCreate.title: Create a new evolution task
evolutionCreate.content: Click the "New Task" button to create a task. Each task corresponds to a complete algorithm evolution workflow.

evolutionTaskConfig.stepperContent: This is the task configuration stepper. Fill in each step sequentially: data preparation, LLM providers, evaluator, evolution algorithm, etc. Click a step name to switch between completed steps.
evolutionTaskConfig.submitContent: After completing each step, click "Next" at the bottom to continue. On the final "Confirmation" step, click "Submit" to start the task.

aiBuild.composerContent: Describe your problem, goals and constraints in natural language here. The AI gathers requirements and builds the pipeline automatically. You can add details anytime.
aiBuild.previewContent: The left panel shows the three-step progress (Analysis → Build → Review) and lists the config and code files the AI generated — click a file name to preview it.
aiBuild.runContent: Once the AI build finishes, this button becomes clickable to submit the task and start the evolution run; it stays disabled until the build is ready.

results.tabsContent: Switch between Simulation / Render / Insights / IDE to view the evolution process, rendered output, analytical insights, or the generated code in the IDE.
results.canvasContent: This shows the whole evolution process. Click any node to see its code, score and parent/child links on the right; hold Ctrl/Cmd to multi-select and compare.
results.actionsContent: View task status and the version tree here. You can View params, Adjust params (copies a new version), and Run / Stop / Re-run the task.

taskRow.content: The task you just created shows up in the left task list. In real projects you'll see every task here — click any row to switch between them.

send.title: Step 3 · Chat with the AI
send.content: The agent gathers your design requirements through a back-and-forth conversation. We've pre-filled the first turn. Click "Send" to start; after a few turns the AI will ask whether to begin building, and sending "Start build" kicks the build off.

building.title: Step 4 · Wait while the build runs
building.content: The left panel is the build pipeline: the progress bar fills as the agent moves through Gathering → Build → Review. Generated files appear in the file list below.

run.title: Step 5 · Submit and start the auto-design loop
run.content: Build is done. Click "Submit & Run" at the bottom of the left panel to kick off the evolution loop — candidate algorithms appear generation by generation.

canvas.title: Step 6 · Watch the design process unfold
canvas.content: While the loop runs you can inspect the evolution graph and ask the agent to analyse it. The tree grows as it goes — every node is one algorithm the system designed.

ide.title: Step 7 · Read the final algorithm
ide.content: Click the IDE tab to see the actual code LLM4AD_Next evolved — in a real run this is the artifact you'd take with you and use.

ideCode.title: Step 8 · Skim the generated code
ideCode.content: This is the algorithm LLM4AD_Next evolved — a greedy nearest-neighbor with 2-opt refinement TSP heuristic. In a real run you can copy it straight into your project, or keep iterating with the AI. Click "Got it" when you're ready to wrap up.

exit.title: You're ready
exit.content: Head back to the project list, configure an LLM provider, and create your first real project. The walkthrough is always one click away from your user menu.

globalConfig.title: Global Configuration
globalConfig.description: Configure LLM providers and default model settings shared across all projects.

addProvider.title: Add a Provider
addProvider.step1: Navigate to "LLM Providers" in the left sidebar.
addProvider.step2: Click "Add Provider" in the top-right corner.
addProvider.step3: Fill in the provider name, select the provider type (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic).
addProvider.step5: Add one or more model names — type a name and press Enter to add.
addProvider.step6: Optionally adjust timeout and max retries.

setDefault.title: Set Default Models
setDefault.step1: On the LLM Providers page, find the "Default Model Settings" section at the top.
setDefault.step2: For each role (Planner, Coder, Report, Other), select a provider from the dropdown.
setDefault.step3: After selecting a provider, choose a model from the available models.
setDefault.step4: New tasks will automatically use these default configurations.

taskManagement.title: Task Management
taskManagement.description: Create, configure, run, and analyze evolution tasks within your projects.

createTask.title: Create a Task
createTask.step1: Enter a project from the Projects page.
createTask.step2: Click "New Task" in the left task list panel.
createTask.step3: Enter a task name and optionally select a template.

configureParams.title: Configure Parameters (Step by Step)
configureParams.description: New tasks enter the configuration wizard automatically. Follow these steps:
configureParams.step1_desc: Upload the required files (fitness function, datasets). Click "Upload Directory" to select a folder, check the files to upload, then confirm. You can edit files after uploading.
configureParams.step2_desc: Select providers and models for the Planner and Coder roles. If left unset, system defaults will be used. You can also click "Configure Providers" to jump to the global provider settings.
configureParams.step3_desc: Configure the fitness evaluation method. Set the evaluation function entry point, timeout, and other evaluation parameters.
configureParams.step4_desc: Choose the evolution algorithm type (e.g. island model). Adjust population size, number of iterations, selection strategy, and other hyperparameters.
configureParams.step5_desc: Configure code generation strategy, prompt templates, and related parameters for the Coder component.
configureParams.step6_desc: Configure memory management, logging, workspace paths, and version control. Default values usually work fine.
configureParams.step7_desc: Review the full YAML configuration. You can edit directly, import/export YAML files. Click "Submit" to start the task.

runTask.title: Run a Task
runTask.step1: After configuring parameters, click "Submit" on the confirmation step.
runTask.step3: Watch the evolution simulation in real-time on the main visualization panel.
runTask.step4: Use the progress bar at the bottom to navigate between generations.
runTask.step5: Click "Stop" in the right panel to halt a running task.

viewResults.title: View Parameters, Results & Logs
viewResults.step1: Click "View Parameters" in the right panel to see the read-only configuration.
viewResults.step2: Switch to the "Logs" tab in the right panel to view real-time run logs.
viewResults.step3: Click nodes in the visualization to view algorithm details, fitness scores, and lineage.
viewResults.step4: Use the trend analysis panel to track score progression across generations.

insightReports.title: Insight Reports
insightReports.step1: Switch to the "Insights" tab in the main content area.
insightReports.step2: Select a report type: Overall Summary, Node Comparison, Chain Analysis, or Optimal Algorithm Analysis.
insightReports.step3: Select the required nodes (varies by report type).
insightReports.step4: Optionally choose a specific provider/model for report generation.
insightReports.step5: Click "Generate Report" and wait for the AI-generated analysis.

versionSystem.title: Task Version System
versionSystem.description: When you adjust parameters and re-run a task, a new version is created automatically.

howItWorks.title: How Versions Work
howItWorks.step1: Each task starts as a root version.
howItWorks.step2: Clicking "Adjust Parameters" on a completed/failed task creates a child version with the same configuration.
howItWorks.step3: The new version can be modified and run independently.
howItWorks.step4: All versions are shown in the Version Tree in the right panel.

versionCompare.title: Version Comparison
versionCompare.step1: Click the "Version Compare" button in the right panel.
versionCompare.step2: Select at least 2 versions (up to 6) by clicking them.
versionCompare.step3: Switch between "Parameters" and "Scores" tabs to compare.
versionCompare.step4: Use grouped bar charts or radar charts to visualize score differences.

versionOperations.title: Version Operations
versionOperations.step1: Click a version in the tree to switch to it.
versionOperations.step2: Edit version tags for easy identification.
versionOperations.step3: The "Latest" badge marks the most recently modified version.
